name: llm_posting_channel_defaults
description: Managed default guidance for LLM posting-channel classification behaviour (agency/recruiter vs direct employer).
lines: Decide who is actually posting this ad: the employer that will hire the candidate directly, or a recruitment agency/staffing firm posting on behalf of a client.

Judge this from the substance of the ad, not from the poster's company name alone — many agencies have generic-sounding brand names (e.g. a name with no word like 'recruitment' or 'staffing' in it) and many direct employers use words like 'talent' in their team names.

agency_or_recruiter: the ad describes itself as representing, partnering with, or working on behalf of a separate hiring organisation (e.g. 'our client', 'on behalf of', 'partnering with a leading [industry] organisation', 'one of our clients', 'searching on behalf of'), or the poster is a named recruitment/staffing/executive-search agency and the employer is described only vaguely or anonymously.

direct_employer: the ad speaks in the voice of the actual hiring organisation about itself (e.g. 'join our team', 'we are looking for', 'at [Company] we ...') with no mention of a separate client being represented.
unknown: use this only when the ad genuinely gives no usable signal either way — do not guess or default to unknown just because the company name is unfamiliar.
confident should be true only when the ad's own wording makes the classification clear; set confident to false when you are leaning one way but the wording is ambiguous or thin.
evidence is one short quoted or paraphrased snippet from the ad (or 'company name indicates agency' style note) that most directly supports the kind chosen; leave it empty only when kind is unknown.
